blocks.heading: Developing a useful questionnaire
blocks.text: Define the research purpose and target respondents before drafting. Use short, neutral questions about one issue at a time, a relevant time period and response options that do not overlap. Include a no-purchase or other option where needed rather than forcing favourable answers. Avoid asking two questions with one answer, such as whether a meal is cheap and tasty. Pilot the questionnaire to find unclear terms and check that answers can be analysed. Keep unnecessary personal information out and explain that responding is voluntary. A well-worded questionnaire still needs suitable respondents; clarity alone does not make a convenience sample representative.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nela Lunches asks nearby workers about weekday collection and meal format at a proposed price of N$35. Model questionnaire: Introduction—Voluntary anonymous study of weekday lunches; select one option unless stated. Q1 In a usual working week, how many days do you buy lunch? 0 / 1–2 / 3–5. Q2 Which format would you prefer at N$35? Box / Wrap / Salad / Would not buy / Other: ____. Q3 Where would you prefer to collect? Workplace collection / Shop / Delivery / No preference. Q4 What time is most convenient? Before 12:00 / 12:00–13:00 / After 13:00. Q5 What one improvement would most affect your choice? ____. Pilot these terms before wider use.
